questions.question_text:
A tree has $9$ vertices.
How many edges does it contain?

options.why: Equated the number of edges to the number of vertices.
Added 1 to the number of vertices instead of subtracting 1.
Subtracted 2 from the number of vertices instead of 1.

questions.solution_text:
A tree with $n$ vertices has $n - 1$ edges.
$\text{Edges} = 9 - 1$
$= 8$

questions.question_text:
A tree network contains $14$ edges.
How many vertices are in the network?

options.why: Subtracted 1 from the edge count instead of adding 1.
Assumed the vertex count equals the edge count.
Multiplied the edge count by 2 using the degree formula.

options.text: It is disconnected and contains a cycle.

options.why: Failed to notice that the graph has 5 vertices and 4 edges ($n-1$).
Confused Eulerian trail conditions with tree requirements.

options.text: It contains multiple edges between two vertices.
options.why: Mistook the 3-cycle for a multiple edge.

questions.solution_text:
$n = 5$
$\text{Required edges} = 5 - 1$
$= 4$
$e = 4$
Although $e = n - 1$, the graph has two disconnected components $\{A, B, C\}$ and $\{D, E\}$ and contains cycle $A\text{–}B\text{–}C\text{–}A$.
The graph is not a tree because it is disconnected and contains a cycle.

questions.question_text:
A connected network has $7$ vertices and $11$ edges.
How many edges must be removed to create a spanning tree?

options.why: Subtracted $n$ from edges ($11 - 7 = 4$) instead of $n - 1$.
Calculated the number of edges in the spanning tree ($7 - 1 = 6$) instead of edges removed.
Selected the vertex count instead of the number of removed edges.

questions.question_text:
A connected graph has vertices $A, B, C, D, E$.
Which of the following edge sets forms a valid spanning tree?

options.why: Contains cycle $A-B-C-A$ and leaves vertex $D$ disconnected from $A, B, C$.
Has only 3 edges for 5 vertices, leaving vertex $E$ disconnected.
Contains 5 edges forming a 5-cycle, which is not a tree.

questions.solution_text:
$n = 5$
$\text{Required edges} = n - 1$
$= 5 - 1$
$= 4$
The edge set $\{AB, BC, CD, DE\}$ contains $4$ edges forming a single path $A\text{–}B\text{–}C\text{–}D\text{–}E$, connecting all $5$ vertices with no cycles.
$\{AB, BC, CD, DE\}$ is a valid spanning tree.

questions.question_text:
An engineer needs to connect $8$ control sensors with cabling so that all sensors are interconnected.
What is the minimum number of cables required?

options.why: Assumed a loop or cycle is required to connect all sensors.
Subtracted 2 instead of 1 from the number of sensors.
Doubled the required edge count using the sum of degrees.

questions.solution_text:
The minimum number of connections to link $n$ items is a tree with $n - 1$ edges.
$\text{Minimum cables} = 8 - 1$
$= 7$

Removing both $DE$ and $EA$ isolates vertex $E$ from the rest of the network.
Removing both $CD$ and $DE$ isolates vertex $D$ from the rest of the network.

questions.question_text:
The sum of the degrees of all vertices in a tree is $36$.
How many vertices does the tree have?

options.why: Found the number of edges ($36 / 2 = 18$) instead of the number of vertices.
Subtracted 1 from the edge count instead of adding 1.
Added 1 directly to the degree sum instead of finding the edge count first.

questions.solution_text:
By the Handshaking Lemma, $\sum \deg = 2e$.
$2e = 36$
$e = 18$
For any tree, $n = e + 1$.
$n = 18 + 1$
$= 19$
